content.text:
# Best Team Chat Tools for a Small Company

Based on current comparisons, here are the top options depending on your team's needs and existing tools:

## Top All-Around Picks

**Slack** — Widely considered the top choice if budget allows.
Slack leads with 800+ integrations
, and it
integrates with many popular workplace tools, with the ability to connect to almost any project management system
. Pricing is flexible:
it's available as a free download, or you can upgrade to $8/month up to custom-priced plans at the Enterprise level

.

**Microsoft Teams** — Best if you're already in the Microsoft ecosystem.
Microsoft Teams integrates seamlessly with Office 365
. It

has the same functionality of Slack and more, with solid video chat capabilities and conferencing integrations, making it a compelling all-in-one solution when coupled with the Microsoft fleet of project management products
. That said, some reviewers note
it might be a bit too robust for small businesses and casual communications

.

**Google Chat** — Ideal for Google Workspace users, since it
works perfectly with Google Workspace

.

## Budget-Friendly / Small-Team-Focused Options

**Pumble** — A strong free option for small and remote teams.
Its robust free plan makes it a great option as a team communication app for small businesses, especially remote and distributed teams.
Notably,
Pumble stands out as one of the few free messaging apps for professional use that don't delete or restrict your chat history.
**Chanty** — Great for lightweight, task-focused teams. It's
perfect for teams with a structured workflow that need a lightweight communication tool to keep everyone on track, especially smaller businesses and startups watching their budgets
. It offers
AI-powered team chat with built-in task management features, and unlimited message history in the free plan
, though
its integration with third-party apps could be more robust, which may be a drawback for teams relying on other productivity tools

.

**Troop Messenger** — Good for small companies wanting security + simplicity. It's

built with a simple user face and incredible UI/UX, perfect for small companies who need an easy-to-use platform, with unique features like "burnout" and "respond later," plus two-factor authentication and end-to-end encryption

.

## For Deskless/Frontline Teams

**Connecteam** —

A strong fit for small to mid-sized businesses in industries like construction, retail, hospitality, and healthcare that rely on frontline or field-based teams, purpose-built for employees who never sit at a desk—like HVAC technicians or cleaning crews

.

## Pricing Expectations

For budgeting purposes:

small businesses typically spend between $3 and $10 per user monthly for team communication software, and many platforms also provide free plans with basic messaging, collaboration, and file-sharing features
. More specifically,
per-user pricing often starts around $3–$4 per month, with entry-level plans going up to $7–$8 per user

.

## How to Choose

The consensus among reviewers is that fit matters more than feature count:
for small and medium businesses, choose a team chat app that's easy to use, well-organized, and available on all devices, particularly if the business doesn't have an IT team
. Also factor in your existing software —
since Slack, Teams, and Google Chat each integrate best with different ecosystems, consider your existing tool stack when choosing

.

**Quick recommendation:** If you already use Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, stick with Google Chat or Teams for seamless integration. If you want the most polished experience and can pay per-user, Slack is the gold standard. If budget is tight, Pumble or Chanty offer excellent free tiers without sacrificing core features.
